problem: A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin $O$ with acceleration, measured in $\text{m}/{\text{s}}^{2},$ $a(t)=2t-5,$ where $t>0$ is the time in seconds. The positive direction is left to right. If the particle has velocity $v=10\,\text{m}/\text{s}$ when $t=6\,\text{s},$ determine the time intervals in which the particle moves to the left.

feedback.problem: A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin $O$ with acceleration, measured in $\text{m}/{\text{s}}^{2},$ given by the function $a(t)=1-2t$, where $t>0$ is the time in seconds. The positive direction is left to right. If the particle has velocity $v=-6\,\text{m}/\text{s}$ when $t=4\,\text{s}$, determine the time intervals in which the particle moves to the right.
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we find $v(t)$ by integrating the acceleration with respect to time:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\int a(t)\text{d}t \\  & =\int (1-2t)\text{d}t \\  & =t-{t}^{2}+C\end{aligned}
$$

To determine $C$, we use the fact that $v(4)=-6.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}-6 & =(4)-(4)^{2}+C \\ -6 & =4-16+C \\ -6 & =-12+C \\ C & =6.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the velocity $v$ of the particle at time $t$ is $v(t)=-{t}^{2}+t+6.$

To find the time interval in which the particle is moving to the *right*, we must solve the inequality $v>0.$ This gives

$$
-{t}^{2}+t+6=-({t}^{2}-t-6)=-(t+2)(t-3)>0.
$$

Plotting the graph of $v(t),$ we get the following picture.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14094087/assets/74db16dc00f5d08637cef02960409b7fd15c4bd3c19f577fa5a1f30ac8c402d3.png)

From the graph, we see that $v>0$ whenever $0<t<3.$
